transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (CSM), Maya Rios (SE) - Redwood; Aisha Patel (Head of ML), Mark Reynolds (CTO), Jenny Wu (DevOps), Carlos Mendes (FinOps) - Lumenix

[00:00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is the Q4 QBR / health check for Lumenix. Quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Aisha: Hi Sofia, hi Ethan, hi Maya. Aisha here.
[00:00:12] Mark: Mark on my side.
[00:00:15] Jenny: Jenny, DevOps.
[00:00:17] Carlos: Carlos, FinOps.
[00:00:22] Sofia: Cool. Agenda: usage, costs, reliability incidents, security updates, roadmap fit, and then next steps. We'll try to keep each section tight.

[00:02:05] Ethan: I'll start with usage trends — we've seen overall token consumption up about 27% month-over-month for the support assistant flows, driven by longer contexts in the customer conversation transcripts. Most of those are hosted API calls.
[00:02:20] Carlos: Yeah that matches our bill, the invoice spiked in late September. We got flagged by finance. There's a 2-day burst where costs doubled.
[00:02:34] Maya: On the burst — early analysis shows repeated long-context calls to the summarization route, which didn't use prefix caching, so KV cache was getting cold each time, pushing more compute.
[00:02:50] Jenny: We did a deploy mid-September that increased context length for debugging; might be related.

[00:04:12] Sofia: Good, so root cause likely config + no caching. We'll put batching and prefix caching recommendations in the follow-up. Quick question to Lumenix: are those summarization calls customer-facing SLA-critical?
[00:04:25] Aisha: Yes for enterprise customers it's part of the SLA, latency < 1s is preferable but more important is consistency. Some customers are sensitive to a single request taking 3-5 seconds.

[00:06:00] Ethan: On latency — 95th percentile sits at ~820ms on hosted endpoints for the last 30 days, with p99 at ~2.4s. We hit a few outliers during the spike.
[00:06:15] Mark: 2.4s is okay sometimes, but p99 correlated with the billing spike which is the problem. We want predictability — that is why we're evaluating Dedicated.

[00:08:00] Maya: For Dedicated, we can lock throughput and pin model variants. Also quantization options can reduce token cost by ~35% on certain workloads. We should run sample runs with your real prompts to see quality impact.
[00:08:20] Aisha: Important: we can't degrade quality for certain enterprise customers. We need an eval against the prompt set.

[00:10:10] Sofia: Understood. We'll run benchmarks and include qualitative evals. Next, security/compliance — any changes on Lumenix side?
[00:10:22] Jenny: We're moving our SSO provider; SAML change planned in early Nov. We also need KMS integration for Private keys for any on-prem or private deployment.
[00:10:35] Ethan: Redwood supports SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations. For Private deployments we can provide customer-managed KMS or HSM options. We'll attach our security pack after the call.
[00:10:50] Carlos: Also please include SOC 2 and ISO docs, and the audit logs retention options.
[00:10:58] Sofia: Yep — will send SOC 2, ISO, and audit log retention matrix.

[00:13:12] Maya: Back to costs — there are quick wins: enable prefix pooling (cache), reduce max context for non-critical flows, and use batching for async endpoints. With modest config changes we've seen 20-40% cost reductions for similar workloads.
[00:13:28] Carlos: That would help. Is there an automatic suggestion engine in the Console?
[00:13:33] Ethan: Redwood Optimize gives recommendations; we can export suggested profiles and apply in staging. We'll include an initial config file you can drop into staging.

[00:16:05] Mark: About Dedicated pilot: what's the minimum commit? We need numbers to take to procurement.
[00:16:12] Sofia: Typical pilot is a 3-month reserved capacity with an option to scale. We'll send a tailored quote but rough ballpark based on your baseline + 25% headroom.
[00:16:25] Carlos: Ballpark is fine for now; procurement needs exact numbers later.

[00:18:40] Aisha: Reliability incidents — we logged two incidents in August/September. Can you walk through root causes?
[00:18:48] Maya: One incident was a region failover where a noisy neighbor on shared capacity caused degraded throughput; the platform routed to fallback model which had slightly different tokenizer settings and produced formatting diffs. Second incident was a spike in input length causing memory fragmentation on the runtime and increased latencies.
[00:19:05] Jenny: The formatting diffs caused support tickets. We need stronger compatibility guarantees on model fallbacks.
[00:19:13] Sofia: Good point. We can configure model variant mapping so fallbacks are constrained to tokenization-compatible families, and set automatic rollback of response format if regressions detected.

[00:21:30] Ethan: Observability — we've created per-route dashboards for you. You should be able to see token-level cost, latency percentiles, and tracing hooks that map to request IDs.
[00:21:39] Mark: Can we get a CSV export for the last 90 days?
[00:21:44] Ethan: Yes, we'll attach an export and the dashboard link.

[00:24:00] Maya: On model recommendations — your support assistant workloads are a good fit for a 7B-13B quantized variant for most flows. For the high-safety enterprise prompts we might keep a 30B float run or a higher-precision quantized variant. We'll show tradeoffs in the benchmark.
[00:24:22] Aisha: Important: the enterprise prompts include PII detection steps; we need to ensure any quantization doesn't change recall for those detectors.
[00:24:33] Maya: We'll include recall/precision checks in the eval.

[00:27:10] Carlos: Cost anomaly — would using a different pricing tier for embedding vs generation help? Some of our flows combine both.
[00:27:20] Sofia: Yes — we can split routes and route embeddings to a cheaper instance family. Smart routing by policy (cost vs latency) can reduce overall spend. We'll propose routing rules.

[00:30:00] Jenny: A quick ops note — our DevOps team prefers infra-as-code for any config changes. Can Redwood provide a terraform module or API so we can automate?
[00:30:09] Ethan: We have an API and a terraform provider in beta; we'll share docs and sample templates.

[00:32:55] Mark: Roadmap alignment: what features in the next quarter might matter to us?
[00:33:02] Sofia: In the next quarter we have: improved model fallback compatibility, expanded quantization profiles, a new billing export format, and a Dedicated pilot onboarding playbook. Also improved prefix caching UI in Console.
[00:33:18] Aisha: The fallback compatibility is high priority for us.

[00:35:40] Maya: For the pilot scope, propose: 1) baseline performance run on Hosted with current prompts, 2) Dedicated run with pinned model and quantized variant, 3) qualitative eval against your prompt set (safety/PII checks), 4) cost delta analysis and runbook for failover.
[00:35:56] Sofia: That matches what we've used in other pilots. How does that sound to Lumenix?
[00:36:05] Carlos: Sounds good. We need the business case numbers.
[00:36:10] Jenny: Also a staging test that simulates the spike pattern we saw in September.

[00:38:00] Maya: We can reproduce that with a traffic replay if you provide logs; otherwise we can approximate based on anonymized distributions.
[00:38:07] Jenny: We'll share logs — anonymized.

[00:40:30] Ethan: Questions from your side?
[00:40:36] Mark: What's the rollback policy if we see quality regressions after switching to quantized models?
[00:40:42] Maya: We recommend an automatic canary rollout with A/B traffic split and a white-box regression detector. If the detector fires, automatic rollback to previous variant happens and we'll alert your on-call.

[00:42:55] Aisha: On compliance — when we evaluate Private deployment we need to know support SLAs, patching windows, and data residency controls.
[00:43:05] Ethan: Private comes with a support add-on and patch cadence options. Data residency can be in region X or a customer-managed VPC. We'll include the details in the follow-up docs.

[00:46:20] Carlos: Financially — assuming a 25% reduction in token costs via batching + caching, plus 10% overhead for Dedicated reserved pricing, what is rough net? Can you give a sample TCO?
[00:46:35] Sofia: We'll prepare a TCO spreadsheet showing hosted vs dedicated vs hybrid with conservative numbers — deliver with the cost breakdown.

[00:49:00] Maya: A couple of implementation risks: 1) some edge prompts are highly sensitive to tokenization changes, 2) traffic replay might reveal custom post-processing assumptions. We'll flag those early.
[00:49:12] Aisha: We have a small set of high-sensitivity prompts — we'll annotate them and share during the pilot.

[00:51:30] Sofia: Recap: Redwood will send — cost/usage spreadsheet, batching and prefix caching recommendations, security pack (SOC2/ISO/audit logs), Dedicated pilot proposal and quote, benchmarking plan. Lumenix will send — spike logs, high-sensitivity prompt list, procurement window and budget constraints.
[00:51:55] Carlos: Agreed.
[00:52:10] Jenny: We'll get logs to you by Oct 6.
[00:52:18] Maya: I'll schedule a 2-hour benchmark run and share results by Oct 14.
[00:52:25] Sofia: And we'll aim to have pilot kickoff week of Oct 18; Ethan will own the calendar.

[00:54:00] Ethan: I'll send invites and follow-up items after this call.
[00:54:10] Mark: Thanks everyone, helpful sync.
[00:54:15] Aisha: Thanks all.
[00:54:20] Sofia: Thanks, we'll follow up with docs. Bye.

End of transcript.
